title: India Anchors Two of the World's Top 6 Migration Corridors
excerpt: The UN's World Migration Report 2026 confirms India-UAE and India-US corridors among the globe's most powerful human mobility routes.
body:
The United Nations agency on migration just handed India a striking distinction: two of the world's six busiest migration corridors begin in the subcontinent. The IOM's *World Migration Report 2026*, released on May 6, 2026, places both the India-UAE and India-US corridors firmly inside the global top ten.

**What the numbers show:**
The India-UAE route ranks fifth globally, driven overwhelmingly by migrant workers — with more than 3 million Indians making up the UAE's single largest nationality group. The India-US corridor sits sixth worldwide and claims the title of second-largest North American migration route, behind only Mexico-US. Approximately 3.2 million Indian-born migrants lived in the United States in 2024, making them the second-largest foreign-born community in America after Mexicans.

**Why this corridor punches above its weight:**
The IOM singled out Indian-Americans for their outsized influence on bilateral policy, noting their role in shaping trade agreements, defence cooperation, and visa frameworks between Washington and New Delhi. Indian migrants in the US also rank among the most educated foreign-born groups anywhere — 77 percent of those aged 25 or older hold at least a bachelor's degree. Back home, that mobility translates into economic muscle: India pulled in $137.7 billion in remittances in 2024, the highest total ever recorded by any country, surpassing every other nation by a wide margin.

**What to watch next:**
With US visa backlogs for Indian nationals stretching decades and Gulf labour reforms accelerating, policymakers on both corridors face growing pressure to modernise pathways — and the IOM report will likely sharpen that debate in coming months.
